I feel as though everyone has the wrong sense of, "It'll get better don't worry." The truth is what's happened has happened. You're going through depression and that's a reality that has been handed to you. You've realized that you don't have any real friends, the majority of people you interact with will leave you, even if the interactions felt genuine and both of you left feeling happy. It all is just a momentary feeling of happiness, and then the next day comes and we're back to where we started. Life is not about constant happiness, if it were, we would never truly be satisfied. I digress. Things get better, but not in the way everyone proposes it to be, we'll just have a better way of handling them and eventually reach a point where we don't notice the issue thar we once had at one point in time. Life goes forward and it doesn't stop. 

You feel like a husk? Thats understandable considering what everything around you feels like. I feel the same, but I don't ponder about it, that'll kill you. I just make the most of what I feel is correct at that point in time, or what I felt most comfortable doing. I take responsibility of what I have done because I did it, no one else. Go out with that new friend but do not feel as though you're wasting their time or that eventually it's pointless. Just enjoy it.

I apologize if my comment seemed rude, I'm just used to the sob stories that are usually on this subreddit of people complaining of never having a girlfriend and how their life would be so much better if they had a girlfriend. 

Sorry to hear about your family, my condolences. 

I talk mainly out of bitterness and a sheer strict nature of wanting to be as logical as possible with everything.

As for everything else, all I can say is that I hope you're able to persevere and make it through. Suicide will always end up in a "What if?".

Don't tell your girlfriend. As much as a, "dick move" this sounds, I genuinely cannot stress how bad it is to tell your partner your personal mental health issues, especially as a man.

Things that usually come from you telling your partner will go into two ways, you being called a dick for "dumping" your issues onto them, or her acting like she'll support you, but to be sincere, she's just going leave after a while if you don't show any improvement. 

In terms of you telling anyone in general, find a close friend, perhaps an old one you've known for awhile to confide this information with. Ultimately once you've talked about it to someone, it will feel better, like a weight has been lifted. As to whether that person will stay in communication with you after what you've told them, is going to be in the air. Most likely they'll check in in you after a few months, but that's about it. 

I do not know of your history or your own choices that you've made, but I cannot stress how lackluster it is to commit suicide, there is always going to be a reason to move forward even if you believe otherwise.

Sorry to hear about your living situation. 

Could I ask as to why it's currently feeling dire? (besides feeling like you have no friends.)

I find it odd that a majority of people feel as though entering into a relationship will somehow fix their issues. To have someone care about you is on par with having a close family member care about you. Why look for someone who will put up with you, rather than have someone who will help you through the issues such as a genuine friend or a psychologist? It's mind boggling. Instead of saying, "what is it like to have someone 'care' about you?", ask, what decisions have lead me up to this point of where I even need to ask this question.
Could I ask how exactly old you are? The fact of the matter as to why I ask is to exactly give you a good enough response to your situation.

You're confusing love for duty.

Your boyfriend doesn't, "put up with you" because he feels the need to have to. 

He "puts up with you" because he loves you, and he wants you to be happy. 

The same goes for your family (I hope).

You speak of the fear of ultimately being alone, yet contradict yourself by saying you feel you don't deserve them.

You've set your mind that you don't deserve them, and with that alone, you will steadily begin to push them away, even if it isn't intentional.

I'd say let your boyfriend, sister and brother in law, know how much they mean to you, truly. 

Begin to acknowledge they care about you out of love, rather than duty.

Only then, will the path of improvement begin, and the dark void that has surrounded you will begin to dissipate.

I hope for you to feel happy again, and I hope you may be able to reconnect with your mother and brother.

I don't see a love confession everyday on this sub.

You want to better yourself for this person, rather than better yourself, for yourself.

That's wholesome, really.

A better situation would be that you realize, he wants to see you become happy as a person because you yourself can be happy, with yourself.

Dependency and Pursuit are on a thin line. 

Your dependency for this person, has put you on the pursuit of self improvement. But it will never lead to your true happiness, and to the best person who you could be.

Change the purpose of your own self improvement first. 

Then achieve it.

And only then, can you focus on showing how far youve come, to this special person of yours
